doc.title: Roland Hanna interviewed by Monk Rowe, Scottsdale, Arizona, April 15, 2000

title: Civil rights era
summary: Hibbler marched; Hanna gave only lip service and admires those who risked their lives.

story.theme_name: Race and segregation in the jazz life
story.community_name: Politics, race and the state of the country

blocks.x: Well those were active days too, in civil rights.

Yeah there was a lot going on in those days, and Hibbler took part in some of that walking. I never did, I didn’t take any part in any of that except to give lip service. But I think those people did a fantastic job to lay their lives on the line to get people to recognize that hey, the Civil War is over a hundred years. Forget about that stuff. I don’t know if they’ll ever forget it.
